instructions: On Sunday, or up to 5 days ahead: Heat the oven to 375°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, whisk the 1 cup flour, 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp salt.
In a large bowl, stir the 1 1/2 cups bran cereal into the 1 cup buttermilk. Leave it for 10 minutes, until the cereal has softened.
Meanwhile, peel and grate the apple and the carrot. Chop the 1 cup walnuts.
Add the 1/3 cup oil, the egg, 2/3 cup brown sugar, 1 tsp vanilla, the apple, the carrot and the walnuts to the bran bowl. Stir until combined.
Add the flour mixture and stir until there are no dry streaks. Stop there. Any longer and the muffins come out tough.
Divide the batter between the 12 cups. This makes 12 muffins.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick in the middle comes out clean.
Let them cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then lift them onto a rack to cool completely.
They keep in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 5 days. For the freezer, transfer them into a freezer container. They keep for up to 2 months.
In the morning, take a muffin from the fridge and eat it cold, or microwave it for about 20 seconds. From the freezer, thaw one in the fridge overnight, then microwave it for 20 seconds.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the batch on Sunday, or up to 5 days ahead, and keep them in the fridge or freezer.
method_notes: Both soak bran cereal in liquid and bake at 375°F. Small Town Woman (the lead) soaks the cereal in buttermilk and adds grated apple, carrot and walnuts to an all-purpose flour batter, and gives the storage times. Recipe Girl uses whole wheat flour, raisins and orange juice, and rests the batter overnight, which makes it a 4 of 5 from only 4 ratings. Kevin Is Cooking would not load. This one follows the lead.
